DIAGNOSTIC: Think of a time when you noticed something that others had overlooked. Write an essay explaining what you noticed, what you did, and what the experience taught you. Use specific details and organize your ideas clearly.
MOCK 1: If you could add one new class to your school day, what would it be and why?
MOCK 2: Think about a time when you began with one plan but learned something that made you change it. Write an essay explaining the situation, what new information or experience changed your thinking, what you did next, and what you learned about making decisions. Support your ideas with specific details.
MOCK 3: Imagine that you may place one ordinary object from life today in a time capsule for students to open one hundred years from now. Choose the object, explain what it would teach them about daily life now, and describe how you would present it so they could understand its importance. Use specific details and organize your ideas clearly.
